rare.why: DWDS: elevated, dated: break out (a passion)
DWDS: rare: knock down, plough up (separable); wrap lines of text (inseparable)
DWDS: archaic: be lacking (es gebricht an)

forms.ex: Er hat sich beim Skifahren das Bein gebrochen.
forms.exEn: He broke his leg skiing.

forms.en: break, fracture (of a bone); breach (of a promise); fraction (maths)
forms.clue: the fracture; a breach (of a promise)
forms.ex: Der Arzt hat einen Bruch am Arm festgestellt.
forms.exEn: The doctor found a fracture in the arm.
forms.note: The bare stem with a vowel change: brech becomes Bruch.

forms.en: break off (ist); stop, abandon (studies, a trip; hat); abort (a program)
forms.clue: to break off; to drop out of (studies)
forms.ex: Er hat sein Studium nach zwei Semestern abgebrochen.
forms.exEn: He dropped out of university after two semesters.
forms.why: ab = off: you break something off before the end.

forms.ex: Der Abbruch der Verhandlungen hat alle überrascht.
forms.exEn: The breaking-off of the talks surprised everyone.

forms.en: set off (ist); break open (a door, a lock; hat)
forms.clue: to set off; to break open (a lock)
forms.ex: Wir brechen morgen früh in die Berge auf.
forms.exEn: We're setting off for the mountains early tomorrow.
forms.why: auf = up, open: you break a lock open, or break camp and set off.

forms.en: departure, setting off; a new beginning
forms.ex: Kurz vor dem Aufbruch hat es angefangen zu regnen.
forms.exEn: Just before we set off it started to rain.

forms.en: break out (a fire, a war, a disease); escape (from prison)
forms.clue: to break out (a fire, a war)
forms.ex: In der Küche ist ein Feuer ausgebrochen.
forms.exEn: A fire broke out in the kitchen.
forms.why: aus = out: something breaks out of its limits.

forms.ex: Nach dem Ausbruch des Vulkans mussten viele Menschen fliehen.
forms.exEn: After the volcano erupted, many people had to flee.

forms.en: break in, burgle; fall through (ice); slump (prices)
forms.ex: Letzte Nacht sind Diebe in unser Haus eingebrochen.
forms.exEn: Last night burglars broke into our house.
forms.why: ein = in: you break your way into a house.

forms.ex: Die Polizei untersucht den Einbruch in der Bäckerei.
forms.exEn: The police are investigating the break-in at the bakery.

forms.ex: Der Einbrecher ist durch das Fenster gekommen.
forms.exEn: The burglar came in through the window.

forms.en: interrupt; break off (a journey, a call)
forms.ex: Bitte unterbrich mich nicht, wenn ich spreche!
forms.exEn: Please don't interrupt me when I'm speaking!
forms.why: unter = between: you break into the middle of something.

forms.ex: Nach einer kurzen Unterbrechung ging das Konzert weiter.
forms.exEn: After a short break the concert went on.

forms.en: do (something wrong), be up to (mostly joking); commit (a crime)
forms.clue: to do wrong (what have you done?)
forms.ex: Was hat der arme Hund denn verbrochen?
forms.exEn: What has the poor dog done wrong?
forms.why: ver = wrongly: you break the law.

forms.ex: Die Polizei hat das Verbrechen schnell aufgeklärt.
forms.exEn: The police solved the crime quickly.

forms.ex: Der Verbrecher wurde nach zwei Tagen gefasst.
forms.exEn: The criminal was caught two days later.

forms.en: break (into pieces), smash (hat); shatter, fall apart (ist)
forms.ex: Mir ist beim Spülen eine Tasse zerbrochen.
forms.exEn: A cup broke while I was doing the dishes.
forms.why: zer = to pieces: break something into pieces.

forms.ex: Vorsicht, das Paket ist zerbrechlich!
forms.exEn: Careful, the parcel is fragile!

forms.ex: Nach dem langen Lauf ist er zusammengebrochen.
forms.exEn: After the long run he collapsed.
forms.why: zusammen = together: it falls in on itself.

forms.ex: Der Zusammenbruch der Bank hat viele Kunden getroffen.
forms.exEn: The collapse of the bank hit many customers.

forms.en: vomit, be sick (formal, medical; also sich erbrechen)
forms.ex: Der Patient hat in der Nacht zweimal erbrochen.
forms.exEn: The patient was sick twice in the night.
forms.why: Learn it as a word: the formal word for being sick; er- adds no clear picture.

forms.en: snap, break in two (ist: a branch; hat: you break it); break through (the sun)
forms.ex: Das alte Brett ist in der Mitte durchgebrochen.
forms.exEn: The old board snapped in the middle.
forms.why: durch = through: it breaks right through, into two parts.

forms.en: break through (a barrier, a blockade); break (a rule, a pattern)
forms.clue: to break through (a wall, a barrier)
forms.ex: Die Demonstranten haben die Absperrung der Polizei durchbrochen.
forms.exEn: The protesters broke through the police barrier.
forms.why: durch = through: you break your way through something.

forms.ex: Den Forschern ist ein wichtiger Durchbruch gelungen.
forms.exEn: The researchers have made an important breakthrough.

forms.en: open, start on (a packet, a bottle; hat); begin, dawn (a day, an era; ist)
forms.clue: to start on (a new packet); to dawn (a day)
forms.ex: Die Packung Milch ist schon angebrochen.
forms.exEn: The carton of milk has already been opened.
forms.why: an = on, at: you break into a new packet; a new day breaks.

forms.ex: Die ganze Branche befindet sich im Umbruch.
forms.exEn: The whole industry is going through a radical change.
forms.why: um = over: everything is broken up and turned over.

forms.ex: Die Erfindung des Buchdrucks war bahnbrechend.
forms.exEn: The invention of printing was groundbreaking.
forms.why: Bahn = path: breaking a new path for others.

forms.ex: Trotz seiner Gebrechen geht er jeden Tag spazieren.
forms.exEn: Despite his ailments he goes for a walk every day.
forms.why: Learn it as a word: from an old verb gebrechen (to be lacking).

forms.ex: Ihre Großmutter ist alt und gebrechlich geworden.
forms.exEn: Her grandmother has become old and frail.
forms.why: Learn it as a word: from an old verb gebrechen (to be lacking).
